Look for ways to improve the customer's overall technology experience, not just close the immediate ticket. Continually improve technical knowledge and troubleshooting ability. Contribute positively to the Cornerstone team and customer relationships. As a managed IT and cybersecurity services provider, our team works across traditional IT support, networking, Microsoft 365, infrastructure, and cybersecurity. review_candidates.description: Job Number: R0252151 Network Security Engineer The Opportunity: A well-designed secure network is critical to move data and enable the Department of Defense (DoD) to achieve their mission, but how can an organization make sure their network will fit their evolving needs? Crafting the right network with the right equipment and software requires a combination of technical skill and careful planning. That’s why we need a Network Security Engineer like you who knows how to utilize your craft to facilitate the needs of the DoD. As a security engineer on our team, you will work with the DoD to develop a reliable, secure network to support critical missions. You’ll collaborate with SMEs, customers, vendors, and users to learn the strategic goals and operational needs that shape network requirements. You’ll then share your expertise during the planning of acquisition, installation, configuration, and maintenance of network components. From resolving interoperability issues across platforms, to supporting the acquisition of hardware, you’ll put your hardware and software talents to good use. This is your chance to share your experience with backbone networks, cloud technologies, and core networking while broadening your security and network engineering work. You’ll dive into challenging hands-on problem-solving, and encounter opportunities to learn new tools and skills. We focus on growing as a team to make the best solutions for our customers. As a Network Security Engineer at Booz Allen, you’ll design and test new boundary security capabilities in a lab environment and implement newly tested boundary security capabilities into production environments. You will need to support implementation teams with remote network firewall and security appliance support. You will also need to be able to identify and support security requirements for switched and routed networks, and implement network security best practice configuration and associated hardware and software. You'll discover and assess complex client enterprise network deployments, apply leading-edge security principles, theories, and concepts, and contribute to the development of new principles and concepts. You’ll work on unusually complex problems, provide highly innovative solutions, operate with substantial latitude for unreviewed action or decision, and mentor or supervise employees in both company and technical competencies. Work with us as we secure and protect DoD enterprise networks for the better. Join us. The world can’t wait. You Have: 5+ years of experience with network security and the design of IT systems or networks for large commercial enterprises or government agencies 3+ years of experience with firewall and enterprise security design, including device hardening, intrusion detection and intrusion prevention systems, SIEM, firewalls, internet protocol security, and vulnerability assessment Experience with Palo Alto firewalls or Cisco or Juniper firewalls Experience with packet analysis tools, including Wireshark Experience with monitoring tools and log collectors to perform analysis of traffic Experience with boundary protection Secret clearance HS diploma or GED Nice If You Have: Experience designing and implementing cloud-native and over-the-top networking in AWS, Azure, or GCP Experience with SD-WAN Experience with Ansible or Python Experience with public speaking, prior publications, and speaking engagements in industry or vendor forums Knowledge of DoD IT and cloud security policies, including STIGs and DoD Cloud SRG, and how to apply them to the design and implementation of cloud solutions Possession of excellent verbal and written communication skills Clearance: Applicants selected will be subject to a security investigation and may need to meet eligibility requirements for access to classified information; Secret clearance is required. Compensation At Booz Allen, we celebrate your contributions, provide you with opportunities and choices, and support your total well-being. Our offerings include health, life, disability, financial, and retirement benefits, as well as paid leave, professional development, tuition assistance, work-life programs, and dependent care. Our recognition awards program acknowledges employees for exceptional performance and superior demonstration of our values. Full-time and part-time employees working at least 20 hours a week on a regular basis are eligible to participate in Booz Allen’s benefit programs. Individuals that do not meet the threshold are only eligible for select offerings, not inclusive of health benefits. We encourage you to learn more about our total benefits by visiting the Resource page on our Careers site and reviewing Our Employee Benefits page. Salary at Booz Allen is determined by various factors, including but not limited to location, the individual’s particular combination of education, knowledge, skills, competencies, and experience, as well as contract-specific affordability and organizational requirements. The projected compensation range for this position is $99,000.00 to $225,000.00 (annualized USD). The estimate displayed represents the typical salary range for this position and is just one component of Booz Allen’s total compensation package for employees. This posting will close within 90 days from the Posting Date. review_candidates.title: Sr Systems & Cloud Operations Engineer
review_candidates.description: About Us We're rebuilding vertical software with AI — from the inside. Embrace owns the software running inside 16% of the Fortune 500, 45+ state agencies, and 450+ banks and credit unions. We acquire entrenched vertical software businesses and rebuild them around AI — products, operations, go-to-market, all of it. Our Venture Lab launches new AI-native products into those same markets, using the distribution and customer relationships our portfolio already owns. You'll ship AI into production against real workflows, real customers, and a P&L you can see move within a quarter. We hire people who want scope, speed, and ownership, and who are tired of working on AI that never reaches a customer. If you want to spend the next five years shipping into software that already runs the economy, talk to us. Job Description This is a remote position. Hirezon (Interview Exchange) runs hiring, onboarding and HR forms software for higher education institutions. We are part of the Embrace EdTech portfolio. You will own production uptime, backups and recovery for our platform. We are looking for an experienced Systems Administrator with strong production operations experience and broader CloudOps capabilities. Your immediate focus will be Hirezon's production environment, where you will own production uptime, infrastructure operations, backups, recovery and operational reliability. This is a hands-on production role. You will diagnose failures across Windows, SQL Server, infrastructure and Java web applications, recover systems safely, and leave behind runbooks and operational records another engineer can follow. Beyond day-to-day system administration, you will also help evaluate and improve our infrastructure architecture across private cloud and public cloud environments. This includes capacity planning, infrastructure lifecycle management, right-sizing, cost optimization, resilience, automation and identifying opportunities to simplify or modernize infrastructure. The role may also contribute to infrastructure and CloudOps initiatives across other Embrace portfolio companies as needed. Technology you will work with Private cloud and managed hosting environments such as Rackspace; AWS and Azure; Windows Server and Active Directory; SQL Server; Apache HTTP Server and Tomcat hosting Java web applications; SAML single sign-on; CDN and web application firewall platforms; cloud and object storage; monitoring, security and vulnerability management platforms; and infrastructure automation tooling. What you will own Production availability: Monitoring and alerting, incident triage, production troubleshooting, hosting-provider escalations and participation in the on-call rotation. SQL Server operations: Backups and recovery, point-in-time restores, SQL Agent jobs, performance and integrity checks, upgrades, capacity planning and cluster maintenance. Backup and disaster recovery: Regular restore and DR testing, offsite and immutable backup integrity, backup key management, and recovery objectives agreed with the business. Windows and hosted infrastructure: Windows Server, Active Directory, service accounts, clustering, storage, compute, capacity, lifecycle management and infrastructure documentation. Private cloud and CloudOps: Help design and evolve private-cloud and public-cloud infrastructure, including compute, storage, networking, availability, backup and security architecture. Infrastructure planning and capacity: Monitor utilization and growth trends, forecast infrastructure needs, identify capacity constraints, and recommend infrastructure changes before they become production issues. Infrastructure optimization and cost management: Review hosting and cloud utilization, identify underutilized or oversized resources, evaluate hosting alternatives, and recommend opportunities to improve performance, resilience and cost. Infrastructure architecture and modernization: Maintain current-state architecture documentation and help evaluate opportunities to simplify, consolidate, modernize or migrate infrastructure across private cloud and public cloud environments. Web and application tier: Apache, Tomcat and Java runtime upgrades; TLS certificates; DNS and domains. Partner with Engineering on SSO, search-service and application infrastructure upgrades, each with a tested rollback. Security hardening: WAF and firewall rules built in partnership with the security team. Changes should be narrow, tested and reversible, with customer workflows checked before and after implementation. Apply appropriate hardening baselines to servers and infrastructure services. Patching and vulnerability remediation: Regular patch cycles with staged validation, maintenance windows, risk prioritization and rollback plans. Access and secrets: Privileged access, MFA, service accounts, certificates and API keys, with regular access reviews and secure operational practices. Monitoring, logs and audit evidence: Log collection, operational monitoring, incident evidence, infrastructure evidence for SOC 2 and customer security reviews, and corrective actions tracked through closure. Automation and operational standardization: Use PowerShell and other appropriate tools to automate repetitive administration, monitoring, validation, backup and operational tasks. Improve consistency through reusable scripts, checklists and runbooks. Architecture, lifecycle and vendors: Maintain infrastructure diagrams, lifecycle records, renewal tracking, vendor SLAs, capacity plans and hosting/cloud cost reviews. How you will work with others Engineering: Engineering owns application code and releases. You own infrastructure and production operations, and work together on cross-layer incidents, releases and architecture changes. Security team: Security establishes priorities, standards and policies. You implement, validate and operationalize infrastructure security controls. Hosting and cloud providers: You manage operational escalations, understand the architecture of the hosted environments and hold providers accountable to SLAs. Embrace portfolio teams: Where appropriate, you may assist other portfolio companies with infrastructure assessments, CloudOps practices, capacity planning, architecture, operational reliability and cost optimization. Distributed team: Colleagues work across multiple time zones, so operational handoffs, incident records and runbooks must be clear and written. Scheduled maintenance and urgent incidents mean some nights and weekends. Requirements Must have 7+ years administering Windows Server in production for a SaaS, enterprise or hosted application environment. Hands-on SQL Server operations including backup chains, restores, point-in-time recovery, Agent jobs, index maintenance, upgrades and clustering. You have personally restored a production database to a point in time. Windows failover clustering, Active Directory, Group Policy and service-account dependencies. Strong production operations experience, including monitoring, incident response, root-cause analysis, change management and operational recovery. Experience managing compute, storage, networking and capacity in private-cloud, hosted or virtualized infrastructure environments. Apache HTTP Server and Tomcat configuration, including TLS and reverse proxy configurations for Java applications. DNS, CDN/WAF and certificate management using Cloudflare or similar platforms. Strong understanding of WAF and firewall rules, including rule ordering, exceptions, rate limits and false positives. Enterprise vulnerability management and patch-management tools and practices. SIEM, XDR/MDR and log tooling, including analysis, alert tuning and monitoring. PowerShell scripting for administration, automation and operational checks, including logging and error handling. Working experience with a public cloud platform such as Azure or AWS, including storage, backup, compute, networking, identity and security concepts. Understanding of infrastructure capacity planning, right-sizing, performance optimization and cost optimization. Experience evaluating infrastructure architecture and making recommendations around scalability, availability, resilience and lifecycle management. Experience with immutable or protected backup storage. Prior SOC 2, HECVAT, GovRAMP/StateRAMP or similar audit/compliance work. Experience managing hosting, infrastructure or cloud providers against SLAs. Calm incident handling and a habit of documenting fixes and turning operational knowledge into runbooks. Clear written communication and handoffs across teams and time zones. Availability for night/weekend on-call and scheduled maintenance. Nice to have Experience designing or operating private-cloud, VMware, hosted or hybrid-cloud infrastructure. Azure and/or AWS architecture experience beyond basic administration. Cloud and infrastructure cost-management experience, including right-sizing, reserved capacity, storage-tier optimization and vendor cost analysis. Infrastructure-as-Code or configuration-management experience such as Terraform, Bicep, CloudFormation, Ansible or similar. Experience performing infrastructure modernization or cloud-readiness assessments. Experience migrating workloads between traditional hosting, private cloud and public cloud. SAML SSO using Shibboleth or similar platforms, and search platforms such as Solr or Elasticsearch. Enough Java and SQL knowledge to trace an application error into the infrastructure layer and back. Automated backup and restore testing. Experience building infrastructure dashboards, capacity forecasts or operational health reports. First 90 days Weeks 1 to 2: Learn the Hirezon environment, architecture, runbooks and escalation paths. Join the on-call rotation and run the daily backup and production health review. By day 30: Own monitoring and alerting. Complete a point-in-time restore on an isolated server. Own the certificate and domain renewal calendar. Run a patch cycle with validated rollback and participate in a DR exercise. By day 60: Deliver a capacity, infrastructure lifecycle and architecture review covering compute, storage, databases, backups, network dependencies and critical infrastructure risks. Identify immediate reliability, performance and cost optimization opportunities. By day 90: Produce a prioritized infrastructure improvement plan covering operational reliability, capacity, security, automation and cost optimization. Critical runbooks should be usable by a second operator. Establish monthly reporting for backups, recovery tests, patching, certificates, incidents, capacity and infrastructure health. Over time, you will also help establish reusable infrastructure and CloudOps practices that can benefit other Embrace portfolio companies. How we hire Expect a conversation about production incidents you personally handled, infrastructure decisions you have made, and a practical recovery and troubleshooting exercise using sample material we supply. We may also walk through a sample hosted environment and ask how you would assess its reliability, capacity, architecture, operational risks and cost structure. We will ask for references who can speak to your operational ownership. Please do not share confidential information or credentials from another employer. Hirezon is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applicants of every background and do not discriminate on any basis protected by law. Benefits Competitive salary commensurate with experience. Opportunities for career advancement and professional development. Experience collaborating with a diverse, global team. Comprehensive Health Benefits to support your wellbeing and peace of mind.
